extracted.intended_audience: readers/students of classic literature (Rabelais), general readers interested in Renaissance satire and didactic parody
extracted.subtask_description: An excerpt (letter from Gargantua) giving an extensive program and moral advice for educating a noble youth, followed by narrative episodes (meeting Panurge; Pantagruel's disputations). The text mixes practical curriculum prescriptions with moral and social guidance in satirical Renaissance prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages — order and mastery
rubrics_metrics.description: I intend, and will have it so, that thou learn the languages perfectly; first of all the Greek, as Quintilian will have it; secondly, the Latin; and then the Hebrew, for the Holy Scripture sake; and then the Chaldee and Arabic likewise...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame thy style in Greek in imitation of Plato, and for the Latin after Cicero; learn languages 'perfectly' and in that order (Greek first) as the foundation of scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: History and cosmography — memorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Let there be no history which thou shalt not have ready in thy memory; unto the prosecuting of which design, books of cosmography will be very conducible and help thee much.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have histories at ready recall; study cosmography to support historical knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberal arts — geometry, arithmetic, music
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the liberal arts of geometry, arithmetic, and music, I gave thee some taste when thou wert yet little... Proceed further in them, and learn the remainder if thou canst.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue early instruction into full competence in these liberal arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomy — study rules; reject divination/astrology
rubrics_metrics.description: As for astronomy, study all the rules thereof. Let pass, nevertheless, the divining and judicial astrology, and the art of Lullius, as being nothing else but plain abuses and vanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish empirical/technical astronomy from superstitious or divinatory practices and avoid the latter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil law — memorize and philosophically compare
rubrics_metrics.description: As for the civil law, of that I would have thee to know the texts by heart, and then to confer them with philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn legal texts by memory, then interpret and reconcile them with philosophical understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural history — exhaustive knowledge of creatures, plants, minerals
rubrics_metrics.description: I would have thee to study that exactly, and that so there be no sea, river, nor fountain, of which thou dost not know the fishes; all the fowls of the air; all the several kinds of shrubs and trees... all the various metals... together with all the diversity of precious stones...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave nothing of the natural world unknown; comprehensive empirical knowledge of fauna, flora, minerals, and gems is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical and occult texts; anatomy — broad medical learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Then fail not most carefully to peruse the books of the Greek, Arabian, and Latin physicians, not despising the Talmudists and Cabalists; and by frequent anatomies get thee the perfect knowledge of the other world, called the microcosm, which is man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study a wide range of medical authorities (including Jewish/Arabic sources) and obtain practical anatomical experience to know the human microcosm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scriptural study in originals
rubrics_metrics.description: And at some hours of the day apply thy mind to the study of the Holy Scriptures; first in Greek, the New Testament, with the Epistles of the Apostles; and then the Old Testament in Hebrew.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read Scripture in original languages (Greek and Hebrew) as part of disciplined study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral and social formation — virtue, honesty, valour, civility
rubrics_metrics.description: to see thee once in my life completely well-bred and accomplished, as well in virtue, honesty, and valour, as in all liberal knowledge and civility...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education aims not only at erudition but at moral and civic qualities; the student should embody these virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Martial training — chivalry and field exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: as thou growest great and becomest a man, thou must part from this tranquillity and rest of study, thou must learn chivalry, warfare, and the exercises of the field, the better thereby to defend my house and our friends...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine scholarly formation with practical military skills to enable defense and service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disputation and learned socializing — test and display learning
rubrics_metrics.description: very shortly thou try how much thou hast profited, which thou canst not better do than by maintaining publicly theses and conclusions in all arts against all persons whatsoever, and by haunting the company of learned men...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate learning through public disputation (defending theses) and participation in learned circles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious conscience and social comportment
rubrics_metrics.description: it behoveth thee to serve, to love, to fear God, and on him to cast all thy thoughts and all thy hope, and by faith formed in charity to cleave unto him... Suspect the abuses of the world. Set not thy heart upon vanity... Be serviceable to all thy neighbours, and love them as thyself. Reverence thy preceptors: shun the conversation of those whom thou desirest not to resemble...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain piety, humility, charity, prudence about worldly abuses, service to neighbors, respect for teachers, and avoid bad company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filial duty — return for father's blessing
rubrics_metrics.description: When thou shalt see that thou hast attained to all the knowledge that is to be acquired in that part, return unto me, that I may see thee and give thee my blessing before I die.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete studies with the personal filial act of returning to receive paternal blessing; emphasizes duty and timing.
